# atomvm-cbor 0.2.0

This is the first Hex.pm release of `atomvm_cbor`, providing the OTP application `avm_cbor`. Historical Git tag `v0.1.0` remains a source and benchmark baseline and was never published to Hex.pm.

## What is new

- Partial/deferred decoding through `partial_decode/1,2`, `partial_deep_decode/1`, and opaque descriptor accessors.
- Deterministic encoding and strict deterministic input validation, including definite-length enforcement, preferred-width checks, duplicate-map-key rejection, and ordering by original encoded key bytes.
- Preferred serialization support without changing the default non-preferred behavior.
- Bounded full and partial decode with depth, node, total-input, per-string, cumulative-string, and partial-string limits.
- Structured malformed/truncated-input errors across full, sequence, and partial paths.
- One-pass option normalization into fixed internal state, avoiding repeated proplist allocation and lookup in recursive loops.
- Existing public `{text, Binary}`, `{map, Pairs}`, and `{tag, Number, Value}` representations remain supported.

## Host performance

Measurements compare exact historical `v0.1.0` with the audited 0.2.0 implementation on the same host and harness: OTP 29 on arm64 macOS, 31 samples after 1,000 warmups. Values are median/p95 nanoseconds per call; lower is better. The release gate permits at most +5% regression for comparable workloads.

| Workload | v0.1.0 median/p95 ns | 0.2.0 median/p95 ns | Change (median/p95) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| malformed declared array | 350 / 373 | 76 / 80 | 78.29% / 78.55% faster |
| 32-item sequence decode | 1049 / 1122 | 670 / 713 | 36.13% / 36.45% faster |
| nested encode | 1260 / 1324 | 915 / 998 | 27.38% / 24.62% faster |
| nested decode | 440 / 481 | 350 / 386 | 20.45% / 19.75% faster |
| 64-byte string encode | 273 / 301 | 122 / 134 | 55.31% / 55.48% faster |
| 64-byte string decode | 380 / 403 | 163 / 181 | 57.11% / 55.09% faster |
| scalar encode | 231 / 263 | 25 / 30 | 89.18% / 88.59% faster |
| scalar decode | 221 / 256 | 46 / 53 | 79.19% / 79.30% faster |
| partial nested decode | N/A | 363 / 405 | N/A |
| deterministic map encode | N/A | 1565 / 1734 | N/A |
| deterministic map decode | N/A | 759 / 839 | N/A |

## Attached-device performance

The historical and 0.2.0 device measurements use the same CBOR payload, AtomVM 0.6.6 benchmark harness, 50 iterations for common/partial work, and 250 iterations for descriptor accessors after warmup. Historical values are five-run medians; 0.2.0 values are per-call means from the final validation run. They provide measured context, not a same-run statistical gate or a guarantee for other boards.

| Function | ESP32-S3 v0.1.0 µs | ESP32-S3 0.2.0 µs | Change | RP2040 v0.1.0 µs | RP2040 0.2.0 µs | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `encode/1` | 8700.06 | 7160.30 | 17.70% faster | 7193.06 | 5135.80 | 28.60% faster |
| `decode/1` | 8480.04 | 8292.32 | 2.21% faster | 6995.40 | 6439.16 | 7.95% faster |
| `partial_decode/1` | N/A | 11950.84 | N/A | N/A | 9753.54 | N/A |
| `partial_decode/2` | N/A | 12075.74 | N/A | N/A | 9804.06 | N/A |
| `partial_deep_decode/1` | N/A | 10612.50 | N/A | N/A | 8118.06 | N/A |
| `partial_value_bytes/1` | N/A | 769.00 | N/A | N/A | 575.01 | N/A |
| `partial_contents/1` | N/A | 866.97 | N/A | N/A | 501.84 | N/A |
| `partial_skip/1` | N/A | 405.43 | N/A | N/A | 222.60 | N/A |
| `partial_type/1` | N/A | 403.53 | N/A | N/A | 223.81 | N/A |
| `partial_count/1` | N/A | 395.65 | N/A | N/A | 224.82 | N/A |
| `partial_tag/1` | N/A | 460.63 | N/A | N/A | 247.68 | N/A |
| `partial_size/1` | N/A | 469.98 | N/A | N/A | 256.74 | N/A |
| `partial_offset/1` | N/A | 397.17 | N/A | N/A | 227.65 | N/A |
| `partial_length/1` | N/A | 404.78 | N/A | N/A | 232.55 | N/A |

Both attached targets completed the test, benchmark, and 40-round retained-growth soak suites without a watchdog, backtrace, panic, abort, or out-of-memory marker. Early and late heap/memory maxima were flat in the measured soak. This is bounded test evidence, not a claim that the software is leak-free or fully secure.

## Compatibility and packaging

- Erlang/OTP 25 and later.
- AtomVM 0.6.6 validated.
- No runtime dependencies.
- Hex package: `atomvm_cbor`; OTP application: `avm_cbor`.
- HexDocs includes the overview, API guide, changelog, and license.

Rebar3:

```erlang
{deps, [
    {avm_cbor, "~> 0.2.0", {pkg, atomvm_cbor}}
]}.
```

Mix:

```elixir
{:avm_cbor, "~> 0.2.0", hex: :atomvm_cbor}
```

See the public benchmark runner and test suites in the repository to reproduce validation on your own systems.
